opening_message:
Ticket 1: Casey Wu (employee ID E005) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E005.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Casey Wu (E005) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is not permitted; write is the maximum for this employee. Requested write is within policy, recommending write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Casey Wu (E005) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Since training is basic, the maximum is read. Requested write exceeds the maximum, so recommending read.
reason: Conflicting employee facts: HR reports Casey Wu (E005) as full-time (max write for Source Code, since admin requires the Engineer role), while the Security DB reports contractor with basic security training (max read, since write requires advanced training). Given the contradiction, I apply the more restrictive, security-sourced maximum of read. The requested write exceeds that maximum, so the employee is granted read.
